useCase.name: Mark staff attendance by card scan, with a code-verified route when the card is not to hand
useCase.featureRef: 5.6 Barcode, ID-card or QR attendance scanning

intent.name: staff.attendance.manualmark.start
intent.summary: Start a manual staff attendance mark where the card is not to hand, which sends a one-time code to the number on that staff record. One step, and nobody is marked yet.

routesHere: reader is down — begin a code-verified mark for this teacher

request.text: code aa gaya hai, hazri laga do
request.gloss: the code has come, mark the attendance

routesElsewhere.note: The mark is made only when the matching code is entered (BR-7).

request.text: bina code ke hazri laga do
request.gloss: mark the attendance without a code

routesElsewhere.note: A manual mark cannot be made without a matching code. This is the rule that stops anybody being marked present in their absence, and there is no override (BR-7, E7).
The School Admin's ordinary hand-marking route is a different act, made against the staff record rather than verified by code.

request.text: bache ki hazri card se lagao
request.gloss: mark a student's attendance by card

routesElsewhere.note: This route is for staff only. Student attendance is never marked by scanning, whatever the card can do (BR-1).

request.text: card gum ho gaya hai, naya banao
request.gloss: the card is lost, issue a new one

routesElsewhere.note: The use case reads staff cards but does not create or deactivate them, though BR-13 and A2 describe both. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.

steps.note: One step. The code goes to the number held on that staff record and the admin does not choose where it goes (BR-5) — no attendance exists until the code comes back.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A staff record with no contact number, a closed day, an existing scan for the day and an unreachable provider are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the verification with its code sent, and the audit entry. **No attendance record is created** — a manual mark cannot be made without a matching code, and there is no override (BR-7). Every code sent and every resend is logged, so repeated resends against one person can be seen rather than inferred (BR-10).

operations.name: staff.attendance.manualmark.start
operations.idempotencyKey: staff_id + date, since a day carries one pending verification — a repeat resends rather than starting a second
operations.purpose: Begin a code-verified manual mark and send the one-time code to the number on the staff record.

parameters.name: staff_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active staff member matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with department and role.

parameters.notes: The person being marked manually. The code goes to the number on their record and nowhere else (BR-5).

parameters.name: date
parameters.notes: The day being marked. A working day (E3).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Code sent. No attendance exists yet (BR-7).

fields.name: code_sent_to
fields.description: The number on the staff record, masked. Taken from the record and never from the request (BR-5).

fields.name: valid_until
fields.description: The code is valid for a configured period and can be used once (BR-6).

fields.name: resend_count
fields.description: How many times it has been sent, which makes a pattern visible (BR-10).

fields.name: existing_scan
fields.description: Where the staff member already scanned in, with the time (E8). No manual mark is needed.

errors.meaning: The staff record carries no contact number.
errors.note: The code has nowhere to go. Adding a number is a change to the staff record, not a step to chain here.

errors.meaning: The school is closed on that date.
errors.note: No attendance is recorded on a closed day, whether scanned or marked manually (BR-12).

errors.meaning: A scan already exists for the day.
errors.note: The message names the scan time. The staff member is already marked.

errors.meaning: The code could not be sent because the provider is unreachable.
errors.note: Message: "The code could not be sent. Try again, or mark by hand." Marking by hand is UC-05-03 and a different act.

planningRules.rule: Never choose where the code goes. It is sent to the number held on that staff record and the admin does not choose the destination (BR-5) — a code sent anywhere else defeats the whole design.

Never mark anybody without the code coming back. There is no override (BR-7), and this is the rule that stops somebody being marked present in their absence — a request to skip it is a request to defeat the control.
Never start a manual mark for a student. This route is for staff only, whatever the card can do (BR-1).

Report the resend count. Every code and every resend is logged so repeated resends against one person can be seen rather than inferred (BR-10) — a third resend for the same person is worth mentioning.
Never treat CODE_SEND_FAILED as a reason to mark by hand instead. Hand-marking is UC-05-03 with a different source on the record, and the two are distinguishable for good (BR-8).

reversal.statement: An unverified code simply expires or is abandoned — both terminal, and neither creates attendance. There is nothing to undo, because nothing was written beyond the log of the code being sent.

request.text: Miss Nadia card bhool aayi hain, code bhej do
request.gloss: Miss Nadia has forgotten her card, send the code

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch. Today is a working day.

steps.note: The code goes to the number on her record; nothing in the request chooses it (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A code is sent to the number on file, valid for the configured period. No attendance exists yet — she has to supply the code before anything is marked (PR-2).

request.gloss: send the code again, third time

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, on a pending verification.

steps.note: The same call resends rather than starting a second verification.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Resent, and resend_count comes back as 3. Report that (PR-4) — repeated resends against one person are logged precisely so a pattern can be seen rather than inferred.

request.text: code ke bagair hi hazri laga do, mujhe pata hai wo aayi hain
request.gloss: just mark the attendance without the code, I know she is here

steps.note: The plan starts the verification and stops there. There is no capability that marks without a code (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The code is sent. Report that there is no override — a manual mark needs the code back from the staff member themselves, and that is the rule that stops anybody being marked present in their absence.

intent.name: staff.attendance.manualmark.verify
intent.summary: Enter the code the staff member supplies and mark their attendance. One step, and the record shows it was verified by code rather than scanned.
routesHere: the code is 418203 — mark her in

routesHere.gloss: the code is 418203, mark the attendance

routesHere.text: code daal ke hazri mukammal karo
routesHere.gloss: enter the code and complete the attendance

routesHere: verify and record the manual mark

routesElsewhere.note: A code from yesterday cannot mark today (BR-6). Starting again sends a new one.
The record produced here is the same staff attendance record as a manual entry, and is corrected the same way (BR-11).

steps.note: One step. The code must match, and it can be used once (BR-6) — the staff member is the only person who can supply it (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A code that does not match, and a mark attempted with no code, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the staff attendance record, its source marked as verified by code, and the audit entry together or not at all. It is the same staff attendance record as a manual entry, carrying the same codes and feeding the same payroll calculation (BR-11) — but the record shows it was marked manually and verified by code rather than scanned, and the two are distinguishable for good, so a pattern of manual marks can be seen (BR-8).

operations.name: staff.attendance.manualmark.verify
operations.idempotencyKey: verification_id, since a code can be used once (BR-6) and a repeat must not write a second record
operations.purpose: Verify the one-time code and write the staff attendance record.

parameters.name: verification_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No pending verification matches — the code may have expired, or none was started.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with staff member, date and when the code was sent.

parameters.notes: The pending verification, resolved from the staff member and date.

parameters.name: code
parameters.notes: 6 digits, as the staff member supplied them. Passed exactly as given — never re-derived, and never taken from anywhere but the person it was sent to (BR-9).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: record_id
fields.description: The staff attendance record — the same kind a hand entry produces (BR-11).

fields.name: source
fields.description: Manual, verified by code. Distinguishable from a scan for good (BR-8).

fields.name: marked_at
fields.description: When the manual mark was confirmed.

fields.name: verified_by
fields.description: The School Admin who entered the matching code.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Spent. It can be used once (BR-6).

fields.name: manual_marks_this_month
fields.description: How many of this staff member's days were manual rather than scanned, so a pattern is visible (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The code entered does not match.
errors.note: Message: "That code does not match. Ask for the code sent to them." Never retry with a guess.

errors.meaning: A manual mark was attempted with no code.
errors.note: Message: "A manual mark needs a verified code." There is no override (BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never supply or guess the code. It is sent to the staff member and only they can supply it (BR-9) — a code produced any other way marks somebody present without their knowledge.
Never retry a mismatched code. E5 means the digits are wrong, and trying variations is exactly the behaviour the one-time code exists to stop.
Report the manual-mark count for the month. Scans and code-verified marks are distinguishable for good so a pattern can be seen (BR-8), and a staff member marked manually every day is worth noticing.
Never describe the result as a scan. The record shows how the attendance arose, and it matters when it is questioned (BR-8).
Never chain a correction onto the mark. The record produced here is corrected under the Principal's approval like any other (BR-11, UC-05-03 BR-7).

reversal.statement: The record produced here is the same staff attendance record as any other and is corrected under the Principal's approval, never overwritten (BR-11, UC-05-03 BR-7). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: Miss Nadia ne code bata diya — 418203
request.gloss: Miss Nadia has given the code — 418203

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, on a pending verification sent twelve minutes ago.

steps.note: The digits are exactly as she supplied them (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The attendance is recorded with source "Manual, verified by code". It feeds payroll exactly as a scan would (BR-11), but the record says how it arose. Report the month's manual-mark count (PR-3).

steps.note: Passed as given. The API returns CODE_MISMATCH (E5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is recorded. Report that the code does not match and ask the staff member for the one that was sent — never try variations (PR-2), which is the behaviour a one-time code exists to stop.

request.gloss: the code is from yesterday, will it work?

steps.note: Resolution refuses: the verification has expired, so there is no pending one to verify against.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is recorded. Report that a code from yesterday cannot mark today (BR-6) and that a fresh one has to be sent — which is starting the manual mark again.
